answer: The wharf report shows the merge explicitly at each meadow. Because of that, a hostile operator who spins up 36 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 281 times the capital for one share. The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. That is 39 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
